title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page, numbered 169 and headed 'IX', from SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §13, which deals with smooth commutative analytic groups over a complex analytic base. The archive stamp reads 487. The sheet was evidently filed among (or reused as scrap paper for) the 1975–76 notes on divided-power De Rham structures; the neighbouring pages concern 'special De Rham structures', which have nothing to do with it.

Setting (13.1):
- S is a complex analytic space with a point s.
- A is a smooth commutative analytic group over S, with identity component A^o.
- The exponential gives an exact sequence 0 → R → E → A^o → 0. Here E = Lie(A) is a vector bundle and R is the kernel of exp, a sheaf of discrete subgroups (periods).
- The 'dictionary' 13.1.4 identifies homomorphisms A^o → A'^o with O_S-linear maps E → E' carrying R into R'.

13.2 setup:
- For an analytic space X over S, X̂ denotes the formal object obtained from the infinitesimal neighbourhoods S_n of s, i.e. the system X ×_S S_n.
- The page opens by noting that X ↦ X̂ commutes with finite products, so it sends groups to groups.
- X̂ depends only on the restriction of X to an arbitrary open neighbourhood U of s.

Lemma 13.2.1. Assume:
- (a) A is connected;
- (b) R is a constant sheaf near s;
- (c) R_s spans the complex vector space E_s.
Then for any second smooth analytic group A', the map u ↦ û from homomorphisms over the germ (S,s) to homomorphisms of the formal groups Â → Â' over Ŝ is bijective.

Proof begun on the page:
- Homomorphisms from the connected group A factor through A'^o, also after base change to U or to S_n. So one may assume A' = A'^o.
- Via 13.1.4, one must show that a formal homomorphism amounts to a germ of a linear map E → E' respecting the lattices.
- The continuation (not on this page) uses that R is constant and spans E_s. A map on the constant lattice R → R' is rigid, i.e. determined at s and hence on each S_n, and it determines the linear map E → E'.

Purpose: this is a GAGA/rigidity-type comparison used in SGA 7 to compare analytic and formal (e.g. Raynaud/Mumford-type) uniformisation of degenerating abelian varieties and tori near a point.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on the page; the proof is only begun here.
The page is a stray SGA 7 typescript page and is unrelated to the divided-power De Rham notes of cote 136.

ideas.what: Formal completion along a point commutes with finite products and depends only on a neighbourhood of s, so it sends analytic groups to formal groups.
ideas.modern_name: Formal completion functor on analytic spaces

ideas.what: Lemma 13.2.1: for a connected smooth analytic group whose period lattice R is constant near s and spans E_s, homomorphisms over the germ coincide with homomorphisms of formal completions.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / analytic-to-formal comparison for homomorphisms of complex analytic groups (tori)

ideas.what: The exponential exact sequence 0→R→E→A^o→0 and the dictionary between homomorphisms of connected analytic groups and lattice-preserving linear maps of Lie algebras.
ideas.modern_name: Uniformisation of commutative complex Lie groups over a base
